title: Exoplayer download service unable to download different HLS videos with different cookie value for authentication
body: I have implemented a download service and it is working fine with normal HLS URL's....but when i try download a HLS URL which usses some cookie value for authentication...my download fails because download manager initializes only once in download service of exoplayer. Is there any way to restart the service every time or change the instance of download manager every time for each video or to stop the download service if one video has been completed and start service again for another video as that would solve my issue.
author: anandsingh2903

comments.body:
When you subclass the `DownloadService` you need to implement the `getDownloadManager` method. So you can construct the `DownloadManager` yourself.  So your app can determine what `DataSource.Factory` is passed to the constructor of `DownloadManager`. If you pass a `ResolvingDataSource.Factory` you can change the request at the moment when the request is issued. This seems to be a flexible way to change your request.

>  restart the service every time or change the instance of download manager every time

Would the apporach above help for this? Instead of creating a new service or download manager you would be able to change the request you are doing with the `ResolvingDataSource` that modifies the `DataSpec` passed to the upstream data source by consulting the `ResolvingDataSource.Resolver` that you implement.

Please let me know if this helps.

If not, can you clarify a bit how the request to the server needs to be changed for successfully downloading with authentication?
Alright will try your suggested implementation and will get back to you.
This is working great....thanks

satisfaction_conditions: A way to handle different authentication cookies for different HLS video downloads
A solution that doesn't require restarting the download service for each video
A method to dynamically modify download requests at runtime
A solution compatible with ExoPlayer's download service architecture

title: Blank screen while switching video from portrait to landscape full screen for DRM enabled videos in DASH format
body:
Issue description:
While switching a video from portrait to landscape mode a blank black screen is visible for a sec before showing the video frame.This happens while switching from landscape to portrait also.This is occuring only for the videos which are DRM protected.This is seen only in few devices.It appears in the exoplayer demo app as well.

Reproduction steps:
1.In the exoplayer demo app play the video with DASH+DRM
2.Enable auto rotate option in settings.
3.Rotate the phone to landscape.
4.A blank screen is shown for a sec before the video frame shows up.
5.Switch to portrait again and see the same blank screen

Link to test content
You can check any drm enabled video from the demo app for dash stream.

Version of ExoPlayer being used
2.9.0

Device(s) and version(s) of Android being used
1.Mi Note 7 Pro Android version:9.0--Issue arises
2.Asus Zenfone Max Pro M2. Android version:8.0--Issue arises
3.Real Me 2 Pro. Android version 9.0--No issue
4.Lenovo K5 note. Android Version 6.0--Issue Arises
5.Samsung Galaxy J2 Pro. Andorid version 6.0--No Issue
6.Mi A2. Android Version 9.0--No issue
7.Redmi Note 3. Android Version 6.0--No issue 

Could you please check into this issue.
author: meenukrishnamurthy

comments.body: This is a limitation in the underlying platform. The fact that the output path is secure means that the video buffers aren't available to be composited into the rotation animation when the display orientation changes, so for the duration of the animation the surface appears as though it is black. You will observe the issue in all applications that play DRM protected content.
Can you be more specific as to which underlying platform the issue arises.Because i dont see this issue in all the devices.

As above:

> The fact that the output path is secure means that the video buffers aren't available to be composited into the rotation animation when the display orientation changes, so for the duration of the animation the surface appears as though it is black.

I'm not sure why you don't see the issue on all devices, but my best guess would be that your content doesn't require a secure output path in the license policy, and that the devices where you don't see the issue only support L3 Widevine. If that's the case then you could try forcing L3 Widevine on all devices, to see if that resolves the problem.

Alternatively, is it possible the devices where you don't see the issue simply don't animate orientation changes?
Thanks a lot @ojw28 . Forcing to L3 on all devices worked for me.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why the blank screen occurs during orientation changes with DRM content
A clarification on why the issue appears on some devices but not others
A practical workaround or solution to prevent the blank screen during orientation changes

title: Sound stop after a while when looping
body:
### Issue description

Using ExoPlayer 2.8.2 to play a local .m4a sound file in repeat mode, the sound stop after a while (typically a couple of hours). If playing several files simultaneously, each file stop at a different time. No error is reported in neither the player event listener nor the media source event listener.

The error occurs with both `player.setRepeatMode(Player.REPEAT_MODE_ALL);` or by using a LoopingMediaSource object.

When the audio stop, the following lines appears in Logcat:
    1536-1577/? I/AudioFlinger: BUFFER TIMEOUT: remove(4096) from active list on thread 0xf1203680
    1430-1578/? W/audio_hw_generic: Not supplying enough data to HAL, expected position 942828484 , only wrote 934428960

toggling player.setPlayWhenReady(...) does not restore the playback.

We didn't notice this issue (and none of our users complain) with the previous version of ExoPlayer we were using: r2.4.1. Unfortunately it is not possible to roll back as an audio glitch was audible at the end of each loop.

### Reproduction steps

The following code is running in a service:

```
...
dataSourceFactory = new DefaultDataSourceFactory(context, Util.getUserAgent(context, "XXXX"), null);
player = ExoPlayerFactory.newSimpleInstance(context, new DefaultTrackSelector());
MediaSource audioSource = new ExtractorMediaSource.Factory(dataSourceFactory).createMediaSource(audioItem.getUri());
player.setRepeatMode(Player.REPEAT_MODE_ALL);
player.prepare(audioSource);
...
player.setPlayWhenReady(true);
```

Wait until the sound stops

### Link to test content
Sent by email

### Version of ExoPlayer being used
2.8.2

### Device(s) and version(s) of Android being used
Pixel XL simulator with Android Oreo 8.1
Some of our users complained about the same issue on different devices.

### A full bug report captured from the device
Sent by email
author: retameur

comments.body:
I couldn't see any obvious issues with the media or in the bug report.

Please could you try to reproduce this in the ExoPlayer demo app, but modified to set repeat mode, and on a physical device rather than using the emulator? If you can reproduce it please send the bug report. If not, that suggests there's something wrong with the service (perhaps a leak or not holding locks required to keep the device awake). Thanks.

I think the issue here is that there's a discrepancy between the duration declared in the MP4 container metadata and the actual duration of audio after applying the iTunSMPB trimming for gapless playback. I think the actual duration is 18955260 us (this is the declared duration 19017142 us, which is the duration of audio before trimming, minus the duration of 2112 + 617 audio frames at 44.1 kHz, which are trimmed). This discrepancy causes the renderer position to drift slowly away from the expected position based on the durations of earlier loops, until the player stops loading because it permanently thinks it has enough data buffered, at which point audio runs out.

If you have control over the media you may be able to fix the issue by rewriting the duration in the container to take into account trimmed frames, or possibly switching to using edit lists to signal gapless trimming.

The next steps here are to verify the hypothesis by hardcoding the calculated duration and verifying that playback doesn't get stuck, then possibly altering the extractor to update the duration to compensate for audio frames trimmed based on iTunSMPB metadata.

I have been able to reproduce the bug with ExoPlayer Demo 2.8.4 (report sent by email). The playback stops after the same number of loops (which varies with each specific sound file) as in our app. Its 241 for the frogs.m4a file I've sent by email.

We have control over the media, but it is not a solution for us, as the same media are also used for iOS and the Web. And most of the current users have already downloaded the files.

I'm not sure it is related to the iTunSMPB metatag. I've re-encoded the file twice using fdkaac:
    - once with the --gapless-mode option set to 0 (iTunSMPB)
    - once with the option set to 1: ISO standard (edts and sgpd)
The playback of both files fails simultaneously.

As for the steps you are suggesting verifying the hypothesis, I have no idea how to do so.

I have also tested with ExoPlayer demo 2.9.0 and the bug seems to be fixed now (if it still occurs, it is after way more loops). So problem solved. 

Thanks for your help.

Yes, it was fixed by a change in 2.9.0 which prevents the problem you describe. Still, if you want perfect gapless playback of the looped file, you should try to ensure the duration exactly matches the content.

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that prevents audio playback from stopping after extended looping periods
Compatibility with existing media files without requiring re-encoding
A solution that works across different Android devices
A solution that maintains gapless playback functionality

title: VP9 ext crash from libvpx 1.7.0
body:
It seems libvpx 1.7.0 has more neon code added. There was error when I run config. By adding -mfloat-abi=softfp -mfpu=neon to cflag, I have managed to get the so file compiled. However, after the first frame is decoded, the sample app always crashes with: 

com.google.android.exoplayer2.demo A/libc: Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1, fault addr 0x10 in tid 18160 (Thread-1825)

My ExoPlayer version is 2.8.2. The working libvpx is 1.6.2, which is from Jan 2017.
author: blueslabs

comments.body: I think the errors that occur during configuration might not actually be problematic. What do you see if you just ignore the errors during configuration? I tried building with libvpx 1.7.0, ignoring the errors and playing a video with the vp9 extension and it worked.
Thanks! Did a clean build, it works now. -mfloat-abi=softfp -mfpu=neon is actually only required for the current master, otherwise build can fail. 1.7.0 can build without this.

satisfaction_conditions: A working build solution for libvpx 1.7.0 that doesn't crash
Clarification on which compiler flags are actually necessary
Guidance on handling configuration errors during the build process

title: Unable do play content after upgrading to ExoPlayer 2.6.0 from 1.2.X
body:
We were using ExoPlayer 1.2.X for a while now and decided to upgrade to 2.6.0, but our content won't play, returning some toasts:

"Media includes video tracks, but none are playable by this device"

and

"Media includes audio tracks, but none are playable by this device"

We tried playing in several emulators from Android 6 to 8, and on a Samsung Galaxy S8+ running Android 7.0

How to reproduce the issue:

Player Version: 2.6.0
Device: Pixel XL - API 24

1 - Downloand ExoPlayer version 2.6.0 release.

2 - Add the given media uri and drm_license_url using the drm_scheme "widevine" to the media.exolist.json.

3 - Run the ExoPlayer and try to play the media.

The media uri, proxy url and bugreport file were sent to dev.exoplayer@gmail.com

Thank you in advance for the help!
author: Lezherus

comments.body: This happens because we're concluding from the manifest that the stream only supports PlayReady DRM. This is because the manifest contains ContentProtection elements for PlayReady, but not for Widevine. Adding ContentProtection elements for Widevine should resolve this issue.
@ojw28 Thank you for the prompt answer! But now I'm wondering, if that's the case, why does it works on 1.2.X? Did ExoPlayer use to support PlayeReady but now it doesn't?

Both V1 and V2 support PlayReady where supported by the underlying platform. PlayReady is only a requirement for AndroidTV devices, however. Most Android mobile devices don't provide support.

The reason V2 fails and V1 doesn't is just that V1 performs fewer checks prior to attempting to start playback. Which meant it was prone to try and play content in an unsupported DRM scheme and fail in an arbitrary way, but also that it was able to successfully play content in a supported DRM scheme even the scheme was missing from the manifest.

@ojw28 Thank you for the clarification. But we tried using another manifest with the widevine ContentProtection element included and it still doesn't works, but now it returns a different error.

I e-mailed you the bugreport and new manifest link, could you take a look, please?

The updated manifest plays fine if you add the following line of JSON:
```
"extension": "mpd"
```
So it looks like:"
```
{
"name": "XXX",
"uri": "XXX",
"drm_scheme": "widevine",
"drm_license_url": "XXX"
"extension": "mpd"
},
```
The demo app tries and automatically infer the content type from the extension, but in this case the extension is "ism" and the demo app infers that it's a SmoothStreaming stream. Adding the extra line explicitly tells the demo app what the content type is.
@ojw28 Indeed, it played fine, thank you very much for the help! I must admit that I'm impressed with how fast you guys reply to the issues, congratulations on the amazing job, and please keep it up!

satisfaction_conditions: Explanation of why content that worked in ExoPlayer 1.2.X doesn't work in ExoPlayer 2.6.0
Identification of the specific issue preventing playback in the upgraded version
A working solution to enable content playback in ExoPlayer 2.6.0
Guidance on proper content type configuration for the media format being used
